item.description:
OSPOlogy + OSPO Summit China 2026 — Fishbowl Proposal

Title

The Great Divergence: Native Open Source vs. Local Open Source — How Should Enterprises Respond?

Format

Panel Discussion (35 min) — organized as a fishbowl (4 inner seats, 1 open seat for audience)

Category

Open strategy and innovation to prevent involution

Abstract

A structural divergence is quietly reshaping the global open source landscape. On one side is what we call native open source — the global commons governed by community meritocracy, voluntary contribution, and fork-based exit rights. On the other side is local open source — state-sponsored foundations (e.g., OpenAtom), government-certified AI agent registries (e.g., CAICT’s ai.isc.org.cn), and enterprise consortia operating under administrative logic rather than community governance.
